BiblicalUsage: Euarestéō means to please — to gratify entirely, to be well-pleasing. Enoch pleased God, and by faith he was translated; and the sacrifices of doing good and sharing are well-pleasing to God. It is the word for a life God is glad of.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe euarestéō is the measure of a life: not whether I am busy, but whether God is pleased. I hold that Enoch's walk — pleasing God — is the life I want.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
